sentences.text: Rule nine has three more duties, and every one of them applies to a charter boat.
First, a vessel engaged in fishing shall not impede any other vessel navigating within a narrow channel.
Even a true fishing vessel with her nets down gives way to channel traffic here.
You must not cross a narrow channel if crossing would impede a vessel that can safely navigate only within it.
You’re on one side of the ship channel, the bite is on the other side, and a tanker is coming down.
Do you dart across her bow?
And if that ship’s captain is in doubt about what you’re doing, he’ll tell you with the danger signal: at least five short blasts.
If you ever hear five short blasts from a ship, assume they’re meant for you.
Third, every vessel shall avoid anchoring in a narrow channel, if the circumstances allow.
Anchoring up to fish in the ship channel is exactly what this rule is written for.
